 # Image Prompt Rewriting Expert

You turn a user's image request into one long English paragraph that describes the
finished image as if you were looking at it. You are not talking to the user and not talking to a renderer: you are
an observer reporting what is in the frame.

Work through the eight steps below in order. Each step commits one decision; later
steps never revise an earlier one.

## Step 1 — Read the brief and split it in two

List what the user has fixed and what they have left open.

Fixed, and it must survive into your description unchanged: every string of text
they want shown, every named object, every count, every stated colour, every stated
position, and the aspect ratio if they gave one. Copy their text strings character
for character, in their own script, including punctuation and spacing.

A third thing they may give you is an instruction about the job rather than about the
picture — "use double quotes", "no hard-edged blocks", "4K, no noise", "make sure the
text is sharp". That is not content. Obey it silently where it applies and never echo
it: the description states what is in the frame, never what must be done.

Open, and you must decide it: everything they did not mention. A three-word request
and a three-hundred-word request both become a description of the same size, so a
short brief means you are inventing most of the frame, not writing less.

## Step 2 — Fix the frame

Decide the orientation from the subject, then pick the ratio.

If the user states a ratio, use it. Otherwise: `3:2` for anything horizontal and
`2:3` for anything vertical — these are the two defaults and cover most images.
Use `1:1` for a square badge, icon, album cover or single centred emblem, `16:9`
for a wide cinematic or presentation frame, `1:2` or `9:16` for a phone screen or a
tall standing banner. `3:4`, `2:1`, `21:9`, `4:3`, `9:21`, `4:5`, `3:1`, `5:4`,
`1:3` exist but only when the subject or the user really calls for them.

Whatever ratio you settle on shows up in the description only as a word — vertical, wide, square or tall — and never as a numeric ratio, a resolution, or a pixel count.

## Step 3 — Write the opening sentence

One sentence, around twenty words. Name the medium, the style, the subject, and the
background or palette; usually name the orientation too:

`The image is a ⟨vertical / wide / square / tall⟩ ⟨style⟩ ⟨photograph · poster · illustration · scene · portrait · infographic · close-up · graphic · page · card · sheet · logo⟩ of ⟨subject⟩, ⟨the background and its palette⟩.`

`This is a …` or a bare `A vertical realistic photograph of …` work equally well. The
medium noun is the one part that is never omitted.

The style word goes here — realistic, photorealistic, minimalist, flat-vector,
cinematic, watercolour, isometric, editorial, hand-drawn, 3D-rendered, retro. Name
it once here; you may echo it in the closing sentence.

## Step 4 — Inventory before you write

Before any more prose, settle two lists.

Every element that will appear, each with a place in the frame: upper-left,
across the top, on the far right, in the lower-third, in the centre, in front of,
behind, tucked into the corner. You will need eight to fourteen such positional
phrases, about ten typically, and they must reach the corners, the edges and the
centre — not cluster in the middle.

Every piece of text that will be legible in the image, in reading order.

## Step 5 — Walk the frame

Now describe it in order. Which order depends on how the frame is filled.

**If the frame is divided into regions** — a poster, a page, an interface, a layout, a
wide scene with several things in it — walk the regions:

1. The background and the surface it sits on — this comes immediately after the
   opening sentence, not at the end.
2. The top band: headline, header bar, sky, ceiling, whatever occupies the top edge.
3. Down and across the body of the frame: left side, then centre, then right side.
   Give each region one or two sentences.
4. The bottom band: footer, foreground, ground plane, base row.

**If one subject fills the frame** — a portrait, a close-up, a single object — walk
the subject instead: the background and how far it falls off, then the subject's pose
and where it is placed in the frame, then head and face, then body and each garment or
surface, then what is held or touching it, then whatever little is left at the edges.
Keep using positional phrases inside the subject — in the upper-left of the frame,
behind the left shoulder, along the lower edge — so the frame stays locatable.

Roughly a third of your sentences should open on the positional phrase itself —
"On the right side of the frame, …", "In the upper-left corner, …", "Across the
lower third, …" — so the reader always knows where they are looking.

Keep it to one paragraph. Break to a new paragraph only when the image is genuinely
built from stacked regions — panels, cards, sections, slides — and then one
paragraph per region, each opening on where that region sits.

## Step 6 — Set every piece of text

Skip this step if nothing in the image is meant to be read — a third of images have
no legible text at all, and inventing signage for them is a mistake.

Otherwise, for each string from your Step 4 list, in reading order, name where it sits,
what it looks like, and what it says: `a bold black headline across the top reads "…"`.

Put the string in straight double quotes, in its own script — Chinese, Russian,
Korean, Japanese and Arabic text stays in Chinese, Russian, Korean, Japanese and
Arabic. Give its weight, colour, case and relative size. Describe a line break as a
second line rather than putting a real newline inside the string. If a mark is not meant
to be read — distant signage, a label behind glass, dense body copy — call it
blurred, indistinct, or too small to read rather than inventing letters. If the image contains a chart
or a table, its axes, tick labels, legend entries, series and cell values are text
too: write them out.

## Step 7 — Give the lighting its own sentence

Every image has light in it, and the description always accounts for it: the source,
its direction, its quality, and the shadows and highlights it leaves. Soft diffused
daylight from a window on the left, hard overhead studio light, warm low sun, flat
even ambient light for a diagram.

Once the contents are placed, give it a sentence of its own — `The lighting is …` —
or, if the light is what makes a particular surface look the way it does, fold it into
that surface's sentence. Either way it is stated explicitly, not left implied.

## Step 8 — Close with the whole frame

End on a single sentence that steps back:

`The overall composition ⟨is / uses / feels⟩ …`

`The composition is …`, `The overall design …`, `The overall mood …`, `The overall
palette …` and `The image has …` are the same move. Cover balance and symmetry, the
palette, the style, and the mood in that one sentence. Write exactly one such
sentence — do not follow it with a second summary.

## Throughout

**Size.** The description runs about twenty sentences and four to five hundred words,
roughly twenty-five words a sentence. That is the same size whether the brief was three
words or three hundred: a dense frame with many regions and a lot of text runs longer, a
single quiet subject runs shorter, but a thin brief never buys a thin description.

**Observe, don't instruct.** Present tense, third person, declarative. No "you", no
"create", no "make sure", no "the AI should". No quality boosters — no "masterpiece",
"8K", "highly detailed", "award-winning".

**Hedge what you cannot be certain of.** An observer describing a picture says
"appears to be", "likely", "suggesting", and offers a pair — "a notebook
or a tablet", "wood or dark laminate" — when the thing is genuinely ambiguous. Do
this often; it is the natural register here. Be flatly definite only about what the
user fixed.

**Name colours with a modifier, almost never bare.** Deep navy, muted olive, pale
cream, warm terracotta, soft dusty rose, blue-grey, off-white, charcoal, brownish-
green. Hex codes only if the user gave them.

**Give the material, not just the noun.** Brushed metal, matte plastic, glossy
ceramic, coarse linen, weathered wood, frosted glass, grain, scuffs, condensation,
visible brush strokes, paper fibre.

**Enumerate; never summarise.** "Several items" and "various decorations" are not
descriptions. Say what each thing is. Write small counts as words — three, five,
twelve — and if something is partly hidden, say so and describe the visible part.

**People get their observable surface.** Build, posture, where they are looking,
expression, hair, skin tone, and each garment with its colour and material. Age is a
life stage or a decade — a child, a teenager, a young adult, middle-aged, elderly,
in her thirties — never a number of years. If a face is turned away or cropped, say
that instead of describing it.

**Objects by class, not by brand.** A silver laptop, a mirrorless camera, a compact
hatchback — unless the user named the brand. Photographic and design vocabulary is
welcome: shallow depth of field, bokeh, backlit, close-up, negative space,
grid, drop shadow.

**Everything holds together physically.** Shadows fall away from the light, reflections
match what is in front of the surface, scale is consistent between neighbouring
objects, and a surface reacts to what sits on it. If the user asked for something
impossible, describe it as the image shows it and let the rest of the scene stay
coherent around it.

## Language

The description is always in English, whatever language the request arrives in. The
only exception is text shown inside the image, which stays in its own script.

## Output format

Output the description itself and nothing else: one single paragraph of plain English prose, beginning directly with the opening sentence. Do not output JSON, field names, braces, headings, labels, or any preface or explanation. Do not wrap the whole paragraph in quotation marks.

生成一张高质量中文电商详情页长图，适用于高端保温杯产品，风格干净、真实、有品质感，像真实天猫/京东产品详情页。

产品名称：
“轻量真空保温杯”

内容结构必须从上到下包含：

1. 顶部主KV
- 大幅产品图
- 中文标题：轻量真空保温杯
- 英文小字：Lightweight Vacuum Bottle
- 卖点短句：轻 · 保温 · 防漏

2. 核心卖点区，4个模块：
- 316不锈钢内胆
- 6小时长效保温
- 360°防漏密封
- 轻量便携设计
每个模块都有小图标和一句说明。

3. 产品细节图区
放4张局部特写：
- 杯盖结构
- 密封圈
- 杯口细节
- 磨砂表面质感
要求与主产品一致。

4. 参数信息表
标题：产品参数
内容必须包括：
- 容量：480ml
- 重量：210g
- 材质：316不锈钢 / PP / 硅胶
- 颜色：雪山白 / 深海蓝 / 砂岩灰
- 尺寸：65×220mm

5. 使用场景图
展示办公、通勤、户外三种场景。

6. 底部加入品牌说明小段落。

整体要求：
长图结构完整，模块层次清晰，图文并茂，像真实高端电商详情页，不要杂乱，不要夸张营销风。

I first separate what is fixed from what is open: the request is in Chinese, and it fixes a premium e-commerce long poster for an insulated bottle. It fixes the product name "轻量真空保温杯", the English subtitle "Lightweight Vacuum Bottle", the selling line "轻 · 保温 · 防漏", four core modules, four detail close-ups, a parameter table, three use scenes, and a brand paragraph. It also fixes the strings "316不锈钢内胆", "6小时长效保温", "360°防漏密封", "轻量便携设计", "产品参数", "容量：480ml", "重量：210g", "材质：316不锈钢 / PP / 硅胶", "颜色：雪山白 / 深海蓝 / 砂岩灰", and "尺寸：65×220mm". The clean realistic premium page style is fixed, while exact layout, photography, icons, colors beyond product finishes, lighting, and brand wording remain mine to design.

For the canvas, I choose a tall vertical long-page frame because the subject is an e-commerce detail page with stacked sections. No ratio is stated, so I use a phone-screen-like tall banner ratio rather than a normal portrait photograph. The long structure needs enough height for hero, feature cards, detail grid, specifications, scenarios, and footer without crowding.

My opening sentence carries the vertical orientation, realistic commercial style, poster medium, and the white stainless-steel vacuum bottle subject. I set the background as a warm off-white product-detail surface with dark navy typography and restrained gray dividers. That first sentence establishes the premium marketplace tone before any individual module appears.

Before writing I settle the inventory: across the top goes the hero area, on the left go the main title stack, and on the right goes the large bottle. Under the title sit the English subtitle and selling line, below them a thin divider, then four equal feature cards across the upper-middle row. The middle section holds a centered details heading, four rounded close-up photographs in a two-by-two grid, and their labels beneath each image. Lower down, the left side carries the parameter table, the right side carries three color bottles, then three scenario panels run across the next band, and the bottom edge holds the brand statement; I count thirty-five legible text placements.

I walk the frame as stacked regions because this is a page layout, not one isolated object filling the whole view. The background comes first as a quiet matte surface with fine horizontal rules, generous margins, and consistent spacing that makes the page feel expensive. Across the top, I place the hero bottle on the right with metal hardware, loop handle, water droplets, and blurred outdoor mountain atmosphere behind it. On the left of that same band, I reserve clear negative space for the hierarchy of headline, subtitle, selling phrase, and rule. In the second band, I make four rounded feature cards equal in size, each with a circular icon, a bold title, a smaller explanation, and a restrained border. In the detail band, I keep the four close-ups physically consistent with the hero bottle, assigning cap mechanics, gasket material, rim finish, and frosted body texture to separate images. In the specification band, I balance the table against the color lineup so the information feels practical rather than decorative. In the scenario band, I divide office, commute, and outdoor scenes evenly, each showing the same bottle in believable hands or backpack placement. Along the bottom, I add only a small logo mark and a compact brand paragraph so the page ends quietly.

The text, in reading order, starts in the hero with a large dark navy headline "轻量真空保温杯", a smaller gray subtitle "Lightweight Vacuum Bottle", and a spaced selling line "轻 · 保温 · 防漏". The four feature cards read left to right with bold titles "316不锈钢内胆", "6小时长效保温", "360°防漏密封", and "轻量便携设计", each followed by smaller copy "食品级 316 不锈钢，安全健康", "真空锁温技术，保温保冷持久", "一体式密封圈，倒置放置不漏水", and "轻量机身，约 210g，轻松随行". The details section uses the centered heading "产品细节", then the four captions "杯盖结构", "密封圈", "杯口细节", and "磨砂表面质感" beneath their matching close-ups. The specification section sets the heading "产品参数", table rows "容量：480ml", "重量：210g", "材质：316不锈钢 / PP / 硅胶", "颜色：雪山白 / 深海蓝 / 砂岩灰", and "尺寸：65×220mm", plus color labels "雪山白", "深海蓝", and "砂岩灰" under the bottles. The scenario section reads "使用场景", with panel labels "办公", "通勤", and "户外"; the footer places "品牌说明" at left and the body sentence "我们专注于高品质生活配件的研发与制造，以简约设计和精湛工艺，为日常饮水体验带来轻盈、安全与便利。" beside it.

For the light, I use soft diffused studio daylight from the upper left, strongest in the hero bottle and detail photographs. It leaves mild shadows under cards, gentle highlights along brushed metal edges, and readable sheen on droplets without harsh glare. I give lighting its own sentence because the premium realism depends on consistent softness across photography and interface elements.

I close on the whole page feeling balanced, orderly, and quietly premium, with realistic product photography held inside a clean commercial grid. The final impression should be trustworthy and high-end, like a polished marketplace detail page rather than an exaggerated advertisement.
</think>

The image is a vertically oriented Chinese e-commerce product-detail poster for a white stainless-steel vacuum insulated bottle, presented on a warm off-white background with soft studio lighting, thin gray divider lines, and a clean commercial layout. On the right side of the hero area, a large realistic product photograph shows a matte white cylindrical bottle standing upright, occupying roughly the right third of the composition. The bottle has a smooth frosted-metal body, subtle condensation droplets, a silver brushed-metal lid, a flip-top drinking spout, side latch hardware, and a looped carry handle made of pale metallic or cream-colored material. The background behind the bottle is softly blurred with muted outdoor tones, suggesting mountains or rocky scenery under diffused daylight.

Directly below the hero area, four rounded rectangular feature cards are arranged horizontally with pale borders and white interiors. The first card contains a circular outline icon of stacked metal sheets in dark navy, with the bold title "316不锈钢内胆" and smaller explanatory text "食品级 316 不锈钢，安全健康". The second card contains a circular outline thermometer icon, with the bold title "6小时长效保温" and smaller text "真空锁温技术，保温保冷持久". The third card contains a circular outline water-drop icon, with the bold title "360°防漏密封" and smaller text "一体式密封圈，倒置放置不漏水". The fourth card contains a circular outline feather icon, with the bold title "轻量便携设计" and smaller text "轻量机身，约 210g，轻松随行". All icons use a minimal line-art style, dark navy strokes, and are centered above their corresponding text blocks.

A thin horizontal divider separates the feature cards from the next section. Centered below it is the section heading "产品细节" in dark navy, flanked by short thin horizontal lines on both sides. Beneath this heading is a two-by-two grid of rounded-corner photographic close-ups. The upper-left close-up shows the bottle cap and drinking mechanism from a low angle, including the silver metal rim, flip-open spout, latch, and loop handle against a warm beige background; its caption below reads "杯盖结构". The upper-right close-up focuses on the bottle mouth area, showing the black circular sealing ring inside the opening, the inner dark cavity, and the matte white exterior; its caption reads "密封圈". The lower-left close-up shows the cup rim and drinking spout edge with water droplets visible on the inner surface, emphasizing the smooth interior and sealed construction; its caption reads "杯口细节". The lower-right close-up shows the bottle body texture, with scattered water droplets on the matte frosted white surface and soft shadows around the cylindrical form; its caption reads "磨砂表面质感".

Another horizontal divider introduces the specification section. The centered heading reads "产品参数" in dark navy, again framed by short thin lines. On the left is a light-gray bordered table with five rows, each paired with a simple outline icon in the far-left column. The first row uses a flask-like capacity icon and reads "容量：480ml". The second row uses a weight icon and reads "重量：210g". The third row uses stacked-layer material iconography and reads "材质：316不锈钢 / PP / 硅胶". The fourth row uses a painter-palette color icon and reads "颜色：雪山白 / 深海蓝 / 砂岩灰". The fifth row uses a ruler icon and reads "尺寸：65×220mm". To the right of the table are three small upright product renderings of the same bottle in different colors, aligned horizontally: a matte white bottle labeled "雪山白", a deep blue bottle labeled "深海蓝", and a light gray stone-toned bottle labeled "砂岩灰". Each bottle has the same metallic lid, flip-top spout, side latch, and loop handle.

Below the parameter area, a further divider leads into the usage-scenario section. The centered heading reads "使用场景" in dark navy with thin decorative lines extending left and right. Three photographic panels appear side by side. The left panel shows an office desk scene with a laptop keyboard, notebook, pen, and the white bottle standing nearby; a hand holds a takeaway coffee cup, and the scene is softly lit with a professional indoor atmosphere. Its label reads "办公". The middle panel shows a commuter or traveler holding the white bottle near a dark backpack or bag in an urban setting, with blurred buildings and street elements in the background; its label reads "通勤". The right panel shows an outdoor rocky landscape with mountains in the distance, where a hand holds the white bottle against a natural trail or hillside environment; its label reads "户外".

At the bottom, a final footer-like brand statement area sits on the same warm off-white background. On the left is a small dark navy geometric brand mark resembling a stylized angular emblem. To its right, the bold heading reads "品牌说明". Full body text as follows: "我们专注于高品质生活配件的研发与制造，以简约设计和精湛工艺，为日常饮水体验带来轻盈、安全与便利。" The overall design uses realistic product photography, soft shadows, rounded cards, minimalist line icons, restrained gray rules, and a premium neutral palette dominated by white, navy, silver, and warm beige. The product surfaces are emphasized through close-up textures such as brushed metal, matte powder-coated finish, silicone sealing parts, and water droplets. All product renders and photos show the same bottle consistently, reinforcing a lightweight, insulated, leak-resistant daily-use accessory theme.
